A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable, including their appendices, and describe the same KRLM study. Corresponding methods, equations, figures, and tables can be matched reliably despite appendix renumbering and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original KRLM benchmark results, component ablations, parameter studies, and case/error analyses across inductive and transductive knowledge-graph tasks.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds computational-cost measurements, sparse-graph evaluations, quantitative distortion measurements, and alternative-backbone experiments.

M1.justification: The PAA tokenizer, knowledge encoder, memory-augmented attention, next-entity predictor, scoring combination, and mutual-distillation objective remain unchanged. New explanatory appendices and alternative-backbone evaluations do not establish a revised procedure.

E1.justification: Appendices J.4–J.5 add FB15k237_10, FB15k237_20, and FB15k237_50 and test queries under full versus sparse background graphs. These extend graph-density conditions within an existing domain; the original datasets and task families remain.

E2.justification: The named baseline suite is retained. However, v2 Table 14 adds a 'Supervised SOTA' comparator for dense FB15k237, absent from v1 Table 1's transductive comparison; the specific supervised method is not identified.

E3.justification: v2 adds paired full/sparse background-graph evaluation with a Distortion Rate metric, end-to-end comparisons using Mistral-7B and Llama-3.1-8B on four retained datasets, and resource benchmarks including inference at batch size 16 on one A100. Original benchmark metrics and training schedules remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses investigate sensitivity to graph sparsity, ranking deterioration when contextual evidence is reduced, dependence on the LLM backbone, and computational bottlenecks. These substantially extend v1's retained component ablations, hyperparameter studies, and memory-recall error analysis.

E5.justification: v2 introduces ± reporting for instruction length, forward TFLOPs, and inference latency, and specifies averaging TFLOPs over 100 steps. It does not add seed counts or uncertainty estimates for benchmark accuracy, and the meaning of all ± terms is not explicitly defined.

E6.justification: Original benchmark, ablation, and easy/hard results are unchanged, but substantial cost, sparsity, distortion, and backbone results are added. Table 15 reports DR values of 297.01 for KRLM, 471.42 for ULTRA, and 612.78 for PROLINK. Sparse-graph rankings are mixed: Table 14 gives KRLM Hit@10 of 0.424 versus ULTRA's 0.436 on FB15k237_20.

T1.justification: v2 formally defines DR as mean positive ground-truth rank deterioration. Appendix G.2 revises the entity-GNN bound from O(S(|E|d + |R|d^2)) to O(S(|T|d + |E|d^2)) and adds an implementation-based O(S|E|d) claim. Existing attention derivations are retained; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about knowledge coordination, constrained entity prediction, scalability, and inductive generalization. Added experiments provide supporting evidence without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: New Appendix E distinguishes entity-set restriction from structural conditioning and notes that out-of-set predictions need not be factually false. Additional discussion interprets sparsity and runtime findings, while Appendix K proposes smaller-LLM rule generation as another future efficiency direction.

D1.justification: v2 documents non-LLM parameter initialization, exact backbone variants, per-batch relational-graph construction, and PyTorch Geometric implementation, alongside parameter, runtime, memory, and FLOP measurements. The first-page code pointer changes to a public GitHub repository, although Section 8 retains the anonymous pointer.

R1.justification: v2 adds Lv et al. (2020), Huang et al. (2026), and Zhuo et al. (2024, 2025a), while removing Trouillon et al. (2016) and Yani and Krisnadhi (2021). The overall positioning relative to structural and LLM-based KGFMs remains stable.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely retained. v2 adds explanatory appendices on instructions and prediction constraints, subdivides the complexity discussion, inserts experimental subsections, and updates affiliations, publication headers, acknowledgments, and some notation and cross-references.

P2.justification: v2 adds seven tables covering costs and supplementary experiments (Tables 3–6 and 14–16), redisplays the instruction schema in a standalone box, and expands the hyperparameter table. All seven original figures retain their content, while several figures and existing tables are relocated or reformatted.

improvement.justification: Measured resource costs and clearer implementation details materially improve practical transparency, while the sparsity and backbone experiments add useful validation without altering earlier results. However, the new DR measures ranking degradation under graph sparsification rather than isolating distortion of intrinsic LLM knowledge, and sparse-graph rankings are mixed. The revision provides a supported but limited overall quality improvement.
